source.title: Palette: A Modular, Controllable, and Efficient Framework for On-demand Authorized Safety Alignment Relaxation in LLMs
source.authors: Qi-Tao Tan; Xiaoying Song; Arman Akbari; Arash Akbari; Yan-Zhi Wang; Xiaoming Zhai; Ling-Zi Hong; Zhen Xiang; Jin Lu; Geng Yuan

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a harmful-prompt SFT baseline and refusal outcomes, bearing directly on harmful fine-tuning, but its setup is domain-specific and uses responses obtained after steering rather than reproducing a stated original recipe.
record.gate_note: The SFT comparator is trained on harmful-domain prompts and its refusal rates are reported in Tables H.1–H.2; those results are recorded below. The paper’s main PALETTE method deliberately trains for authorized domain-specific refusal relaxation, so its results do not establish that safety behavior erodes without that targeted inducement. The paper does not test benign-only fine-tuning, per-token KL by response position, compliant-prefix/suffix/decoding bypasses, or whether a small set of parameters carries safety. Its W/O Adaptation ablation is a purposeful refusal-direction ablation, not a test of those opening-token claims.
record.test_reason: The SFT baseline fine-tunes two safety-trained chat models on harmful-domain prompts paired with compliant responses, then reports refusal rates on every harmful domain (Tables H.1–H.2). That bears directly on V1. The setting is new: domain-restricted harmful SFT, with cross-domain spillover measured. It is not the original recipe, so T3 fits better than T2. The training responses were generated by the steered model itself, and the SFT example count is not stated (training uses 20% of GenHarm data).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude PALETTE selectively relaxes refusal on authorized domains, keeps refusal elsewhere and preserves utility, and composes via LoRA merging. On SFT they say only that it lowers target-domain refusal but needs costly response collection and often degrades utility. They draw no conclusions about shallow alignment.
record.recipe_differences: The paper includes an SFT baseline on harmful-domain prompts, but reports domain-specific conditions and collects training responses after steering away the model’s refusals. The SFT example count is not stated. The main PALETTE method is a different, label-conditioned activation-reconstruction adaptation.
record.method_sensitivity: The SFT refusal effect varies by training domain and evaluation domain; off-target refusal changes range from slight to substantial across the reported conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating a single refusal direction at one layer, without the adapter (Table F.3, W/O Adaptation, LLaMA3.1-8B), drops refusal on all GenHarm domains to 0.0–0.047, with utility nearly unchanged (0.694 vs 0.698).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal on harmful prompts is mediated by a single activation direction whose removal eliminates refusal across domains.

record.problems: The SFT results are only reported for two models in the detailed tables; the number of SFT examples is not stated. Results are averages over three runs, but no error bars or other uncertainty estimates are given. The paper’s SFT responses are generated after refusal suppression, and the conditions are domain-specific.
record.rows_left_out: No SFT refusal-rate cells from Tables H.1–H.2 were omitted. PALETTE, CAST, AutoDAN, and other personalized-safety results were not included as rows because they test targeted authorized refusal relaxation rather than the claim’s general harmful/benign fine-tuning or token-position mechanisms.

untested.parts: No dose-response over a few to a few hundred examples, and the SFT example count is not stated. No general (non-domain-restricted) harmful dataset. No models beyond LLaMA2-7B-Chat and LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct for SFT. No harmfulness score, only keyword-based refusal.
No per-token KL by response position.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks. AutoDAN appears only as a baseline for authorized relaxation.
No test of whether a small set of existing weights or ranks carries safety.

missing.what: Utility cost of harmful SFT: average MMLU/GSM8K utility falls from 0.365 to 0.157–0.197 on LLaMA2-7B-Chat and from 0.698 to 0.271–0.305 on LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct.

record.verdict_notes: SFT training responses were produced by steering away the model's own refusals (Arditi-style direction ablation), so the training data are self-generated compliant outputs. Refusal is judged by keyword matching, with no harmfulness scoring. Results are averages over three runs, with no variance reported. The Qwen models have no SFT rows. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The SFT baseline is tested on domain-specific harmful prompts, but the number of SFT examples is not stated; there is no dose-response test across a few to a few hundred examples or a general, non-domain-specific harmful dataset.
No ordinary or carefully selected benign-only fine-tuning condition is tested for harmful-request compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement by response position is reported.
No compliant opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test is reported.
The paper uses a lightweight adapter on one block, but does not test whether a small set of existing weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The study does not test whether a data choice or training objective explains first-token shallowness.
No training intended to spread safety beyond early response tokens, or evaluation of whether such deepening holds up, is reported.

relationships.condition: Harmful SFT on one GenHarm domain, evaluated on that same domain, LLaMA2-7B-Chat and LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct
relationships.reason: On-target refusal falls from about 1.0 to 0.056–0.231 (H1-Vio-Vio, H1-Hate-Hate, H1-Disinfo-Disinfo, H1-Sexual-Sexual, H1-Illegal-Illegal, H2-Vio-Vio, H2-Hate-Hate, H2-Disinfo-Disinfo, H2-Sexual-Sexual, H2-Illegal-Illegal).
relationships.display_finding: On-target refusal fell from about 1.0 to 0.056–0.231 in all five domains for both models.

source_check.reason: Tables H.1–H.2 show substantial on-target refusal reductions to 0.056–0.231 across the ten cited diagonal SFT results.

relationships.condition: Cross-domain spillover between the related Violence and Illegal domains
relationships.reason: Training on Violence or Illegal drops refusal on the other domain to 0.129–0.289 (H1-Vio-Illegal, H1-Illegal-Vio, H2-Vio-Illegal, H2-Illegal-Vio).
relationships.display_finding: Training on Violence or Illegal also dropped refusal on the other domain to 0.129–0.289.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Cross-domain spillover between the related Violence and Illegal domains
source_check.reason: H1-Vio-Illegal, H1-Illegal-Vio, H2-Vio-Illegal and H2-Illegal-Vio show refusal falling from 1.000 to 0.129–0.289.

relationships.condition: Harmful SFT on one domain, evaluated on other, less related harmful domains
relationships.reason: Spillover is uneven. Refusal on non-trained domains often stays at 0.76–0.99, and Sexual drops moderately to 0.41–0.82. Compromise did not generalize to all harmful requests (e.g., H1-Sexual-Disinfo 0.979, H1-Hate-Illegal 0.963, H2-Hate-Vio 0.916, H1-Vio-Sexual 0.536).
relationships.display_finding: Refusal on untrained domains often stayed at 0.76–0.99 (for example 0.979 and 0.963), while Sexual refusal dropped moderately to 0.41–0.82, so the compromise did not generalize to all harmful requests.

relation.reason: The SFT baseline reports the harmful-request refusal behavior named by V1, independently of the proposed PALETTE method.

tranche.reason: Domain-specific harmful SFT in an authorized safety-control setting supplies refusal measurements on trained and other harmful domains, extending V1 to a new setting.

source_check.notes: Refusal is detected using keywords; lower refusal does not independently establish harmful response quality. Exact SFT example counts are not separately specified; Appendix B.2 gives a general 20% training split, and SFT responses are collected after suppressing refusal through steering.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SFT on each matching harmful GenHarm domain, evaluated on that same domain, for LLaMA2-7B-Chat and LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct
reader_labels.reason: Refusal rates fall from the base-model values of 1.000 (or 0.995/0.989) to 0.056–0.231 in the matching domains, showing substantial compliance after the reported SFT conditions; see H1-Vio-Vio, H1-Hate-Hate, H1-Disinfo-Disinfo, H1-Sexual-Sexual, H1-Illegal-Illegal, H2-Vio-Vio, H2-Hate-Hate, H2-Disinfo-Disinfo, H2-Sexual-Sexual, and H2-Illegal-Illegal.
